paragraphs.title: Do Not Rely on the Temple

answers: At the gate of the Lord's house
At the gate of the city
In the valley of Hinnom
easy.explanation: Jeremiah was commanded to stand in the gate of the Lord's house and proclaim God's word.
easy.q: Where was Jeremiah commanded to stand to proclaim the word of the Lord?

answers: Their sacrifices only
Their ways and their doings
The walls of Jerusalem
easy.explanation: The Lord told them to amend their ways and their doings.
easy.q: What did the people need to amend if they wanted to dwell in the land?

answers: Jerusalem
Egypt
Shiloh
easy.explanation: The Lord told them to look at Shiloh and see what He had done to it because of Israel's wickedness.
easy.q: Which place was given as an example of a former holy place that was ruined?

answers: Because the Temple was far from Jerusalem
Because the Temple could not protect those who did evil
Because prayer was forbidden there
medium.explanation: The Temple could not protect people who stole, murdered, committed adultery, and worshipped other gods.
medium.q: Why were the people not to trust the repeated words, “The temple of the Lord”?

answers: A place where sinners hide after doing evil
A cave where Temple vessels are stored
A place where pilgrims gather
medium.explanation: The people treated the house called by God's name as a place of refuge after committing abominations.
medium.q: What does the phrase “a den of robbers” mean in this passage?

answers: Trust in the Temple, sinful deeds, the warning of Shiloh, and possible destruction
Sacrifices, victory, a new Temple, and peace
Exile, return, kingship, and celebration
medium.explanation: Jeremiah warns that the Temple cannot save the people while they continue in sin, using Shiloh as an example.
medium.q: Which sequence of ideas appears in Jeremiah's message?

answers: Increasing the number of sacrifices
Executing judgment and avoiding oppression and idolatry
Building additional temples
challenge.explanation: The promise was connected with amended ways, true judgment, care for the vulnerable, and turning from other gods.
challenge.q: What condition accompanied the promise that the people would remain in the land?

answers: The holiness of a place alone does not prevent its destruction
Shiloh was more important than Jerusalem
The Temple does not belong to the Lord
challenge.explanation: Shiloh shows that even a place where God's name once dwelt could be destroyed because of the people's wickedness.
challenge.q: What does the comparison with Shiloh teach about the holiness of a place?

answers: They avoided the Temple but trusted in it
They sinned and immediately corrected their ways
They committed abominations while claiming the Temple would deliver them
challenge.explanation: They committed evil deeds and then stood in God's house, claiming they were delivered so they could continue sinning.
challenge.q: What was the central contradiction in the people's behavior?

answers: Build an altar
Pray
Call them together
easy.explanation: The Lord commanded Jeremiah not to pray, cry, or make intercession for the people.
easy.q: What did the Lord command Jeremiah not to do for the people?

answers: The children, fathers, and women
The priests only
The king and his soldiers
easy.explanation: The children gathered wood, the fathers kindled the fire, and the women kneaded dough.
easy.q: Who in the family is described as taking part in preparing the idolatrous worship?

answers: Jeremiah
The queen of heaven and other gods
Shiloh
easy.explanation: They made cakes to the queen of heaven and poured out drink offerings unto other gods.
easy.q: For whom did they make cakes and pour out drink offerings?

answers: Because the people were not in Jerusalem
Because the people continued in idolatry
Because there was no altar in the Temple
medium.explanation: The command follows the description of idolatrous worship in the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem.
medium.q: Why would the Lord not hear Jeremiah's prayer for the people?

answers: Liquids poured out as part of worship
Garments worn in mourning
Weapons used in battle
medium.explanation: A drink offering was a liquid poured out as part of a religious ritual.
medium.q: What are “drink offerings” in this context?

answers: Blessing only for the people
Honor for the Temple
Shame, anger, and destruction
medium.explanation: Their worship would bring confusion and shame upon them, while the Lord's anger would be poured upon the land and its living things.
medium.q: What would result from this idolatry according to the Lord?

answers: That the sin had become a family and public practice
That only the women were responsible
That the worship was done secretly
challenge.explanation: Children, fathers, and women all participated, showing that the practice was widespread throughout the household and society.
challenge.q: What does the participation of the whole family emphasize?

answers: Can they harm the Lord?
Does their worship bring them honor?
Do their actions bring shame and harm upon themselves?
challenge.explanation: The Lord says that their actions ultimately provoke confusion and shame upon their own faces.
challenge.q: What is meant by the question, “Do they provoke me to anger?”

answers: Man, beast, the trees of the field, and the fruit of the ground
The Temple only
The prophets only
challenge.explanation: The passage names man, beast, the trees of the field, and the fruit of the ground.
challenge.q: Upon whom would the fire of the Lord's anger be poured?

answers: His voice
The king of Egypt's voice
The priests only
easy.explanation: The central command was, “Obey my voice.”
easy.q: What did the Lord command the people to obey?

answers: He would be their God and they would be His people
They would never need to amend their ways
They would conquer every nation
easy.explanation: The Lord promised, “I will be your God, and ye shall be my people,” if they walked in His commanded ways.
easy.q: What did the Lord promise if the people obeyed His voice and walked in His ways?

answers: They obeyed immediately
They did not listen and hardened their necks
They asked to build another house
easy.explanation: They did not hearken, did not incline their ear, and hardened their neck.
easy.q: How did the people respond to the Lord's words and His prophets?

answers: Sacrifices matter even without obedience
Sacrifices are worthless when people will not obey the Lord
Sacrifices remove the need for prophets
medium.explanation: The Lord emphasizes obedience to His voice rather than reliance upon burnt offerings and sacrifices.
medium.q: What relationship between sacrifice and obedience is taught in this passage?

answers: Their stubborn and sinful desires
Great happiness
Fear of the prophets
medium.explanation: The phrase describes their decision to follow their own stubborn and evil desires instead of God's commands.
medium.q: What does “the imagination of their evil heart” describe?

answers: He sent prophets repeatedly, but the people would not listen
He stopped speaking immediately
He sent only one prophet and gave no warning
medium.explanation: The Lord sent His servants the prophets continually, but the people would not hearken.
medium.q: What pattern characterized the Lord's dealings with the people?

answers: Backward and forward
Right and left
Upward and downward
challenge.explanation: The people “went backward, and not forward,” showing that they were moving away from obedience.
challenge.q: What verbal contrast describes the people's condition?

answers: They rejected repeated warnings, not merely one command
They did not know what the Lord wanted
The prophets never spoke to them
challenge.explanation: The Lord repeatedly sent prophets, yet the people refused to listen and hardened their necks.
challenge.q: What does their response to the prophets reveal about the seriousness of their sin?

answers: It grew stronger through sacrifices
Truth perished and was cut off from their mouth
It passed from the people to the prophets
challenge.explanation: The nation did not obey the Lord or receive correction, and truth had perished from their speech.
challenge.q: How is the people's faithfulness described at the end of the section?

paragraphs.title: Zion's Mourning and the Defiled Temple

answers: Jerusalem
Egypt
Shiloh
easy.explanation: Jerusalem was called to mourn because the Lord had rejected and forsaken that generation.
easy.q: Who was told to cut off her hair and take up a lamentation?

answers: Purifying offerings
Abominations that polluted it
Furniture for their homes
easy.explanation: They set their abominations in the house called by God's name in order to pollute it.
easy.q: What did the children of Judah place in the house called by the Lord's name?

answers: Burned their sons and daughters in the fire
Built a place of worship to the Lord
Buried the prophets
easy.explanation: They built the high places of Topheth to burn their sons and daughters in the fire.
easy.q: What did they do at Topheth?

answers: Because the people had built the Temple
Because the Lord had rejected and forsaken that generation
Because the prophet had left the city
medium.explanation: The Lord had rejected and forsaken the generation of His wrath.
medium.q: Why was Jerusalem called to mourn?

answers: Detestable objects or practices connected with false worship
Musical instruments
Festive garments
medium.explanation: The abominations were detestable objects and practices of idolatrous worship placed in the Temple.
medium.q: What does “abominations” mean in this passage?

answers: Neither was commanded by the Lord
Both were commanded in this passage
Both were meant to correct the people
medium.explanation: The Lord specifically said that the practices at Topheth were not commanded and had not come into His heart; the Temple was likewise polluted by evil.
medium.q: What did the pollution of the Temple and the acts at Topheth have in common?

answers: The house was called by God's name, yet it was polluted with idolatry
Because it was called by God's name, every deed there was acceptable
The house was not called by God's name
challenge.explanation: The passage stresses that the house belonged to God's name, yet Judah polluted it with abominations.
challenge.q: What contrast appears between the Lord's name and the deeds done in the Temple?

answers: That the practice was a special command
That the practice was a sinful human invention never desired by the Lord
That the practice happened only by accident
challenge.explanation: The words make clear that the sacrifice of children was neither commanded nor desired by the Lord.
challenge.q: What does “which I commanded them not, neither came it into my heart” emphasize?

answers: The mourning arises from the gap between the Temple's holy purpose and its sinful use
The mourning was caused by a lack of room for sacrifices
The mourning has no connection with the Temple
challenge.explanation: Jerusalem mourns because a generation rejected by God had polluted the place called by His name.
challenge.q: How is Jerusalem's mourning connected with the defilement of the Temple?

paragraphs.title: The Valley of Slaughter and Destruction

answers: The Valley of Joy
The valley of slaughter
The Valley of Blessing
easy.explanation: The Lord said that the places would be called the valley of slaughter.
easy.q: By what name would Topheth and the valley of the son of Hinnom be called?

answers: They would become food for the fowls of heaven and the beasts of the earth
They would all be buried in the Temple
They would be offered as sacrifices
easy.explanation: The carcases would be meat for the fowls of heaven and the beasts of the earth.
easy.q: What would happen to the carcases of the people?

answers: The voices of mirth, gladness, the bridegroom, and the bride
The voices of the prophets only
The sounds of water and rain
easy.explanation: The Lord would cause the joyful voices of celebration and weddings to cease.
easy.q: Which sounds would cease from Judah and Jerusalem?

answers: Because many houses would be built there
Because it would be filled with graves and corpses
Because songs of joy would be heard there
medium.explanation: The place would be filled with graves and corpses because there would be no place left for burial.
medium.q: Why would the place be called the valley of slaughter?

answers: There would be no room to bury the dead
There would be no room for the Temple
The people would not be able to find the city
medium.explanation: The phrase indicates such a great number of dead that burial places would be exhausted.
medium.q: What does “till there be no place” mean in the context of burial?

answers: The destruction brings both death and the end of ordinary city life
The corpses produce greater celebrations
The two events are unrelated
medium.explanation: The judgment is shown both by the unburied dead and by the disappearance of celebrations and weddings.
medium.q: What connection exists between the corpses and the ending of joyful voices?

answers: A place of forbidden worship would become a symbol of judgment and destruction
The place would become a center of celebration
The place would remain unchanged
challenge.explanation: The place where sinful rites occurred would become associated with slaughter, graves, and divine judgment.
challenge.q: What does the change from Topheth to the valley of slaughter show?

answers: The voices of the bridegroom and bride versus a desolate land
The prophet's voice versus the king's voice
Jerusalem versus Shiloh alone
challenge.explanation: The joyful voices of weddings would be replaced by desolation throughout the land.
challenge.q: What central contrast appears in the final verse?

answers: It affected one place only
It affected Judah's cities, Jerusalem, and life throughout the land
It affected the Temple but not the land
challenge.explanation: The passage describes death, graves, and the silencing of joy in the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem, leaving the land desolate.
challenge.q: How extensive was the destruction described in this passage?
